questions.stem: A team needs to capture events from several sources, filter and route them to different stores, with no code. Which Fabric engine fits?
questions.explanation: Eventstreams are the no-code way to capture, transform and route events in Real-Time Intelligence.

questions.stem: A team already has PySpark code with complex stateful logic and wants to run it on a stream that writes to Delta tables. Which engine fits?
questions.explanation: Spark structured streaming runs code-first stream processing in notebooks or Spark job definitions and writes to Delta tables, so existing PySpark logic carries over.

questions.stem: Streaming events must be stored and queried interactively within seconds using KQL. Where should they land?
questions.explanation: Eventhouses are built for ingesting and querying high-volume event data with KQL in near real time.

questions.stem: Which two are things an eventstream does? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Run any Python library on each event
Route one stream to more than one destination
Ingest events from Azure Event Hubs

questions.explanation: Eventstreams connect to sources such as Event Hubs and send events to one or more destinations, with no-code processing in between. Custom Python and model training belong in notebooks.

questions.stem: Which two needs point to an eventhouse with KQL rather than a lakehouse with Spark? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Time-series analysis such as series_decompose and anomaly detection
Large batch transformations written in PySpark
Ad hoc queries over billions of recent log rows in seconds
Training a machine learning model on a year of history in a notebook

questions.explanation: An eventhouse is built for fast queries and time-series analysis on high-volume event data. Large batch transformations and model training in notebooks are Spark's strengths.

questions.stem: Row-level changes in an Azure SQL database must reach Fabric as a real-time stream, without code, so that they can be transformed and routed to several destinations. What should you use?

options.text: A Spark structured streaming notebook that polls the database
A Dataflow Gen2 with a one-minute refresh schedule
A pipeline Copy activity with a tumbling window trigger
An eventstream with the Azure SQL Database CDC source

questions.explanation: The eventstream Azure SQL Database CDC source captures a snapshot and then every row-level change as events, without code. The other options are code, batch or scheduled copies.

questions.stem: Events already flow through an eventstream. A team has a Spark Structured Streaming notebook with custom logic that should process those events. What should it add to the eventstream?

options.text: A Spark Notebook destination that loads the existing notebook
An Activator destination that starts the notebook
A custom endpoint destination that the notebook polls
A lakehouse destination, after which the notebook runs on a schedule

questions.explanation: The Spark Notebook destination (preview) loads a notebook in the workspace to process the default or derived streams with a Spark Structured Streaming job.

questions.stem: Inside an eventstream, a developer wants to write the stream logic as code, with windowing, joins and aggregations, instead of drag-and-drop operators. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Eventstreams support a SQL operator (preview) for code-first stream processing, including windowing, joins and aggregations. The other items aren't part of an eventstream.

questions.stem: Security logs arrive as semi-structured JSON with long free-text messages, and analysts need fast text search over them as they stream in. Where should the events be stored?
questions.explanation: Eventhouses are the preferred engine for semi-structured and free-text analysis of time-based streaming events.

questions.stem: Sensor events stream into Fabric. When a reading passes a threshold, an operator must be emailed automatically, with no code. Which eventstream destination should you add?
questions.explanation: The Activator destination monitors for conditions and acts, for example by alerting users, when data reaches thresholds. The other destinations store or pass on data.

questions.stem: A team is choosing an eventhouse for streaming telemetry. Which two statements about eventhouses are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: An eventhouse suspends when not in use unless you enable always-on
An eventhouse can hold several KQL databases that share capacity and resources
An eventhouse can hold only one KQL database
An eventhouse is designed for OLTP workloads with enforced foreign keys
An eventhouse stores only structured data, so JSON must be flattened first

questions.explanation: An eventhouse is a container for multiple databases that share capacity, and it suspends when idle unless always-on is enabled. It handles structured, semi-structured and unstructured event data and isn't an OLTP store.
